title: Where did the effect go?
hook: Hold a treatment consequence fixed, then trace which outcome path remains.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: adjusting for a drug's effect on blood pressure hides the drug's effect on strokes.

misconception: Treating don't control the mediator as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: adjusting for a drug's effect on blood pressure hides the drug's effect on strokes.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: A treatment raises mediator M by 2 and outcome obeys Y=3M+T. What total effect follows increasing T from 0 to 1 if you let M respond?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-don-t-control-the-mediator/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Treatment raises mediator M by2; outcome Y=3M+T. Total effect7, direct1, mediated6. Fix M removes6; learner can block or leave mediator path open.

claims.text: Letting M respond retains total effect 7; holding M fixed retains direct effect 1. The mediator carries 2×3=6 units of the stipulated effect.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-don-t-control-the-mediator/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Treatment raises mediator M by2; outcome Y=3M+T. Total effect7, direct1, mediated6. Fix M removes6; learner can block or leave mediator path open.

claims.text: Controlling a treatment consequence removes that pathway from the contrast. A direct-effect question may want that operation, but it is a different question from the total effect and needs its own identification assumptions.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-don-t-control-the-mediator/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Treatment raises mediator M by2; outcome Y=3M+T. Total effect7, direct1, mediated6. Fix M removes6; learner can block or leave mediator path open.

claims.text: Treatment changes M by 3; M changes Y by 2 per unit; the direct path adds 4. What total effect follows? The indirect effect is 3×2=6, plus direct effect 4, giving 10.
